title: [P1] Dashboard auto-refresh: let the operator choose the interval and show a live countdown to the next update
reasoning:
OPERATOR REQUEST (2026-09-24, verbatim): 'it talks about the amount of time in auto refresh it should be changeable and should be counting down so people know how long until the next update comes in'.

MEASURED CURRENT STATE (verified in the tree, not assumed):
- The refresh interval is HARDCODED PER PAGE and the pages disagree with each other AND with themselves. Overview (internal/dashboard/generator.go:524) renders 'htmx live · 10s' while line 526 of the SAME page renders 'auto-refresh 60s' — two contradictory claims on one screen. health.html:1 and :24 poll 'every 10s'; queue.html:31 and tick_history.html:3/:39 poll 'every 30s'.
- There is NO operator control: no select, no input, nothing persisted. The refresh rate is whatever the template was compiled with.
- There is NO countdown: the labels are static prose ('auto-refreshing every 10s...', 'updating in 30s...') that never changes, so the operator cannot tell when the next update actually lands, or whether the page is still live at all.
- The stale prose also lies after a manual navigation: 'updating in 30s...' keeps asserting 30s even in the last second before the swap.

WHY IT MATTERS, not just cosmetics: the operator's whole workflow on this surface is 'watch the fleet and react'. Without a countdown there is no way to distinguish a slow page from a frozen one, and with the hardcoded 10s/30s split the operator cannot slow a heavy page down (the overview is 358KB / 622 rows and re-renders on every poll) or speed one up when they are watching a change land.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. ONE interval control, presented on every page (not per-page hardcoding), offering at least: 5s, 10s, 30s, 60s, 5m, and Off.
2. The chosen interval PERSISTS across pages and reloads (localStorage), so the choice is made once.
3. A COUNTDOWN is visible next to the control, counting down in seconds to the next update and RESETTING on each actual swap — so it reads as live, not as static prose.
4. Off must genuinely stop polling rather than merely hiding the label; the countdown must then say so (e.g. 'paused') instead of counting.
5. The contradictory 'htmx live · 10s' / 'auto-refresh 60s' pair on the overview is DELETED — one page, one stated cadence, and that cadence is the one the countdown is counting to.
6. The default must match the fastest lane's real need (10s) and must not regress the existing behaviour for an operator who never touches the control.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (not binding): the polling sites currently use htmx 'every Ns' triggers. A single driver that dispatches one named event on the body, with the partials listening via 'hx-trigger="autorefresh from:body"', gives one code path for the interval, the persistence and the countdown, instead of five hardcoded values that each need editing.
acceptance: one persisted interval control + a live countdown on every page; Off truly stops polling; the contradictory per-page interval prose is gone

title: [P1] Tick-report delivery modes: full body | markdown attachment + header/footer | link only
reasoning:
OPERATOR REQUEST (2026-09-24, verbatim): 'we want to change the way we get the tick reports. as markdown files so i get the file attached with the text in the attach message of what ran the time just the like header and footer but instead of spamming me in all the channels with long bodies of text i might not read we need to have modes in the system to support sending as a file or just reporting that the tick finished and a link to the tick in the dashboard if i want to open it. the goal is for us to have all 3. write to thread full message, attach file of full message to thread (with link), or last just send the link in the thread that opens up directly to the report.'

MEASURED CURRENT STATE (read in the tree, not assumed):
- Delivery is ONE hardcoded shape. internal/scheduler/deliver.go:105 performs exactly:
    hermes send --to <deliver> --subject <subject> --file <tempfile>
  where the tempfile body is trimToolNoise(output) + '\n\n_<tickID> · <trigger>_' (deliver.go:87-88). So every tick pushes the FULL body text into the thread, with no length cap (deliver.go:66 says so: 'No length cap — full detail preserved'). That is the spam.
- The header ALREADY exists (the --subject line, deliver.go:104: '🤖 <project> [<tickID>] · <trigger>') and so does the footer ('_<tickID> · <trigger>_', deliver.go:88). Both are already composed — they just need to be separated from the body.
- The deliver target (projects.deliver, models.go:82) is 'platform:chat_id:thread_id'. There is NO per-lane notion of HOW to deliver, only WHERE.

KEY FINDING — the attachment needs no CLI work: 'hermes send' supports attachments today by putting MEDIA:<path> in the message text (verified in `hermes send --help`: 'To send an image/document as an attachment, use MEDIA:<path> in the message text instead', example 'hermes send --to telegram "MEDIA:/tmp/chart.png"'). A .md extension arrives as a DOCUMENT, not a photo. So all three modes are buildable inside THIS repo; nothing in the Hermes CLI has to change.

GAP FOUND FOR LINK MODE: there is NO configured public/base URL for the dashboard anywhere (only the --listen flag, logged at cmd/schedulerd/main.go:855). A link built from the listen address (0.0.0.0:9090) is unopenable from the operator's phone. A base-URL config knob is therefore REQUIRED for mode 3.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A per-project delivery-mode setting (new column e.g. deliver_mode, settable via the project API/PUT exactly like deliver) with values: full | file | link. DEFAULT and empty = full.
2. full = BYTE-IDENTICAL to today's behaviour. No regression for any lane that never opts in.
3. file = the Thread receives a SHORT message consisting of header + footer only, WITH the complete report as a .md DOCUMENT attachment. The attachment filename must identify the lane and tick.
4. link = the thread receives header + footer + ONE absolute URL that opens that tick's report in the dashboard.
5. Link mode MUST NOT emit an unopenable URL. With no base URL configured it must degrade to full (and log why) rather than send a broken link — decide and document the choice in the row's completion note.
6. Fail-safe: an unknown mode value, or any mode-specific failure, must fall back to full. A tick report must NEVER be silently dropped because of a delivery-mode problem.
7. The attachment must still exist on disk when `hermes send` runs (deliver.go:96 currently defers the os.Remove — the removal must stay AFTER the send returns).
8. deliverAlert (timeout/error notices, deliver.go:115) stays as-is: those are short and must stay visible.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (not binding):
- Put the URL construction behind ONE helper, e.g. tickPermalink(baseURL, lane, tickID), returning the per-tick route when it exists and the lane page until then. SCHED-GAP-1593 adds the per-tick page and SCHED-GAP-1594 covers the push-flag/digest; keeping the URL in one helper means mode 3 does not need rewriting when 1593 lands, which is why this row deliberately carries NO hard dependency on it.
- The seam for tests is the composed `hermes send` argv: assert the args per mode, and that mode=file both writes the .md and includes its MEDIA: path in the body text.
- Reuse the existing temp-file pattern (deliver.go:90) for the markdown attachment rather than inventing a second mechanism.
acceptance: deliver_mode full|file|link per lane (default full, byte-identical to today); file = short message + .md document attachment; link = short message + one openable URL; unset base URL degrades to full; reports are never silently dropped

title: [P1] The drain-restart deploy cannot converge on a busy fleet — it idles the fleet then reaps in-flight ticks as failed(drain_timeout)
reasoning:
MEASURED DEFECT from an operator-ordered deploy (2026-09-24). The sanctioned deploy path (scripts/scheduler-deploy-drain-restart.sh) is pause -> drain (wait for active_ticks=0) -> restart -> resume, with the drain cap resolved to 5h. On a busy fleet that drain cannot converge, so the script either times out having done nothing (it did exactly this on 2026-09-22: 'DRAIN TIMEOUT after 60 min: NOT restarting', active_ticks stuck at 3) or the fleet stays paused for its whole cap.

EVIDENCE COLLECTED LIVE THIS SESSION:
1. Two deploy attempts were SIGTERM'd mid-drain (33 min, then 7 min) by the session runtime - i.e. the deploy never even reached the reap. Not the forkbomb reaper (it logged 'clean' on every run), not OOM, not mem-monitor (a read-only snapshot logger).
2. A manual controlled drain then proved the drain CANNOT converge: active_ticks sat at 10-12 and every one of those ticks was ALIVE and HEARTBEATING within the last minutes (heartbeat_at 14:00-14:02, clock 14:02), with spawned_at up to 127 minutes earlier - i.e. past the 120-minute figure the script cites as the live max effective deadline. Wave-enabled namespaces legitimately use 3-4h effective deadlines, so 'wait for them to finish' means waiting hours.
3. There is NO cancel/kill/drain endpoint on the API (grepped: no route matching cancel|kill|abort|drain|reap|orphan), so in-flight ticks cannot be deliberately ended - only waited out.
4. THE REAL COST, measured after finally restarting with ticks in flight: 40 ticks were reaped as failed with orphan_reason='drain_timeout'. So the pause does not merely idle the fleet; it converts in-flight work into failures. 0 lanes auto-disabled (auto-disable is default off), but 40 spurious failures is a real statistical and compute cost per deploy.
5. Fleet is busy enough that active_ticks=0 is not a state you can wait for: ~186 ticks completed in one hour around this window, with 10-12 concurrently running at any instant.

WHY IT MATTERS: every restart redeploys HEAD (ExecStartPre), so fixes only take effect at a restart. If the only restart path idles the whole fleet then marks 40 ticks failed, every future fix carries that cost, and operators are incented to skip deploys - which is exactly how a merged fix sat undeployed here while the operator reported the same bug three times.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (any coherent subset, decided explicitly rather than by default):
1. A documented restart path that does NOT require the fleet to reach active_ticks=0. Options to evaluate: (a) an explicit 'restart now, accept N reaps' mode that PREDICTS the reap count and requires confirmation with that number; (b) a deliberate drain that CANCELS in-flight ticks with a distinct reason (e.g. 'operator_restart') so they are not indistinguishable from genuine failures in the failure-rate stats; (c) per-namespace draining so a restart waits only on the lanes it must.
2. drain_timeout failures must NOT be counted as lane failures. A tick the operator's deploy killed is not evidence the lane is broken. Verify how recent_failures / failure-rate consume these rows and exclude operator-induced reaps.
3. The runbook must state the true mechanism: on THIS unit, `kill $MainPID` does NOT restart it (the unit has no Restart=always) - the scheduler stays DOWN. The working verb is `systemctl --user start coding-hermes-scheduler`. This was discovered the hard way (the scheduler was down ~1 minute this session).
4. The deploy script's 5h cap must be reconciled with the real cost of holding the fleet paused: at ~186 ticks/hour, a 5h drain can forfeit more work than the deploy delivers.
5. Whatever is chosen must be REHEARSED against a busy fleet, not reasoned about: the 2026-09-22 timeout and this session's two killed attempts both looked fine on paper.
acceptance: a restart path that does not need active_ticks=0; operator-induced reaps excluded from lane failure stats; runbook states the real start verb; rehearsed on a busy fleet
